translations.translatedText: # Wednesday 12.2.2020 (radio)

Bernie Sanders won the primary election in New Hampshire. The government proposes that people can visit a nurse for free. Almost all children get vaccinations. More and more men are not doing military service.
## Bernie Sanders won the New Hampshire primary
![Bernie Sanders ](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11204325)
Open image viewer
Bernie Sanders. Photo: Justin Lane / EPA
In the USA, Bernie Sanders has won the Democratic Party primary in the state of New Hampshire.
Bernie Sanders got 26 percent of the votes. Pete Buttigieg came second. He got 24 percent of the votes. Counting of the votes is still a little unfinished.
Buttigieg and Sanders also did best in the Iowa primary.
In the primaries, the Democrats choose their candidate for the presidential election next November.
## The government proposes free nurse visits
![Sign of a health centre on an outside wall](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_2560,h_1440,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-5974995d9c317924f62/1570517417)
Open image viewer
The new law is meant to take effect at the beginning of next year.. Photo: Pyry Sarkiola / Yle
The government proposes that people can visit a nurse without paying. The aim is that everyone can easily go for care.
At the moment, visits to a nurse do not cost anything in any Finnish municipality. About 40 percent of municipalities charge a fee.
In some municipalities, a nurse visit costs over 20 euros. The most common fee is about 11 euros.
The reform does not remove doctor's fees. The law is meant to take effect at the beginning of next year.
## Few babies in Finland go without vaccination
![A baby is given a vaccine in the upper arm. ](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11202735)
Open image viewer
A baby's first vaccine is given in Finland at the age of two months. Photo: Rex Features / AOP
Almost all children in Finland get the most important vaccinations.
About 1 percent of children under 3 years old have no vaccinations at all.
Over 98 percent of children born in 2017 have received the vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough and polio.
96 percent have received the vaccine that protects against measles, rubella and mumps.
Finland's national vaccination programme offers free vaccinations against 12 diseases to children and young people.
## More and more men are skipping military service
![Conscripts in combat exercise in the Defence Forces' Kaakko 19 main military exercise .](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11204871)
Open image viewer
The biggest reason for not doing conscript service is mental health problems. Photo: Antti Aimo-Koivisto / Lehtikuva
More and more men are not going into the military.
Nowadays about every third man does not do military service. The reason is often mental health problems.
Petri Hulkko, commander of the Army, says that many people feel anxious living together with other people.
The Army is planning new tasks for the military. The aim is that more men than now can do military service.
## The Chinese Formula 1 race is postponed
![Formula 1 Shanghai](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11194712)
Open image viewer
The Formula 1 Chinese race in Shanghai is postponed because of the coronavirus. Photo: Getty Images
The Chinese Formula 1 race is postponed. The reason is the coronavirus.
The 4th race of the Formula 1 series was meant to be run in Shanghai on 19 April. An attempt is being made to find another date for the race.
